impunity

im-PYOO-nih-tee -- stress on the second syllable, PYOO. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Impunity is freedom from punishment or harm.

For a decade the gang operated with impunity, protected by officials who looked the other way.

Example

In a video game with all penalties switched off, a player runs every red light and crashes into everything in sight with total impunity, respawning instantly. Nothing he does costs him a thing.

Impunity is complete freedom from punishment or consequence. Notice the shape the word takes in real sentences -- impunity almost never appears alone. It lives inside the phrase 'with impunity.'

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

immunity: Immunity is protection granted to a particular person by someone with the power to grant it -- a witness given immunity cannot be charged for what she admits. Impunity is nobody granting anything: punishment simply never arrives. Immunity is a shield handed to you; impunity is the strange freedom of acting where no penalty follows.

pardon: A pardon is official forgiveness that arrives after the offense -- one act, formally wiped away by someone with the authority to do it. Impunity needs no one's signature: the wrongdoer keeps acting, and punishment never comes at all. A pardon closes one case; impunity means there was never a case to close.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

accountability: being answerable for what one does

punishment: a penalty imposed for wrongdoing

Where it sits · how wide the freedom from consequences runs

exemption → impunity → license

exemption vs. impunity: Exemption is narrow and official -- it frees you from one particular rule -- while impunity is wide open: nothing you do gets punished at all.

license vs. impunity: License runs even further than impunity in one direction: impunity means you escape punishment for what you have done, while license means you now feel free to do whatever you like, precisely because no one will stop you.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — im-: not (the form in- takes before p) (Latin in-)

root — pun-: punishment (Latin poena 'penalty' / punire 'to punish')

suffix — -ity: forms a noun: the state or condition of (Latin -itas, via Old French -ite)

Put it together: Impunity is this unit's prefix in its im- form (in- shifts to im- before p) plus pun- ('punishment') plus the noun-making -ity. Read straight through, it names 'the condition of not being punished.' The same root is doing obvious work in punish, punitive, and -- through Latin poena -- in penalty.

Use the root in a new word: punitive: The league's new punitive measures take effect at the start of next season.

Root Check

Word Choice

Impunity is a noun, and in real writing it lives inside one phrase: With impunity. You will almost never see 'an impunity' or 'her impunity' -- you will see 'he broke the rules with impunity,' 'they polluted the river with impunity.' Learn the phrase, not just the word, and remember that it is a noun: the adjective form of this idea is 'unpunished.'
